source_refs.excerpt:
M4: ingest from communication data — Record layer, Slack adapter, evidence lifecycle

The engine's goal is memory over a team's real communication; until now the
only entry was a pre-built EpisodeCard. This milestone adds the layer below.

- Record contract generalizes ChatMessage: container/thread identity, author
  kind, permalink, reactions, edit and revocation timestamps. record_id is
  namespaced (container:native_id) and validated — Slack's ts is unique only
  within a channel, and two channels' identical timestamps collapsing into one
  source_id would corrupt INV-5's shared-evidence count and merge unrelated
  matters. A golden case now proves cross-channel same-ts is never shared
  evidence.
- INV-11 (new, normative): an edited source is a new observation — a new
  assertion alongside the old one, distinguishable by recorded_at; a deleted
  source revokes evidence — no assertion or interval is removed, but query
  results carry evidence_status so a conclusion resting on revoked evidence is
  visibly flagged instead of silently persisting or vanishing. SourceRef
  gains uri so P5's promise ends at a clickable permalink.
- Slack adapter (pure, no LLM): conversations.history and message events to
  Records — mrkdwn unescaping and entity resolution, Block Kit, bot vs human
  authors, thread identity, permalink construction, non-conversational
  subtypes filtered so they never become evidence.
- Thread-first identity: a thread is the default matter boundary; cross-thread
  merging still requires the INV-5 evidence floor.
- Wired in: engine.add_records, mh extract, MCP add_records (8 tools), REST
  /v1/add_records, with per-container sync watermarks. Re-syncing an
  overlapping window is a complete no-op and does not re-invoke the model.

Verified: 159 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17 (40 golden cases);
narrow-terminal run green; ruff clean; the Slack fixture example runs end to
end with readable excerpts and clickable evidence.

source_refs.excerpt:
fix(ci): make lint and the CLI tests pass outside a developer machine

The first CI run failed on lint and on all three Python versions while the
cross-backend Postgres conformance gate passed. Both causes were real: a gate
that cannot pass is not a gate.

- ruff had never been run; it reported 78 errors. All are resolved, with the
  ruleset pinned in pyproject so local and CI agree. Six narrow noqa comments
  and one per-file ignore remain, each for a case where the rule is wrong about
  this code (Typer declares CLI metadata through argument defaults, and the
  tool-error boundaries deliberately catch broadly); the ruleset was not
  weakened to reach zero.
- tests/test_cli.py invoked '<repo>/.venv/bin/mh', so the nine CLI tests could
  only pass on a machine with a repo-root virtualenv. On CI, and for anyone who
  ran pip install, they failed with FileNotFoundError. They now resolve the
  entry point the way an installed user does, and 'python -m matterhorn.cli' is
  supported and covered.

The three Python versions had failed identically, so 3.11 support was never in
question.

Verified after the autofixes: ruff exits 0, 141 tests green across SQLite and
PostgreSQL 17, and the invariant probes still hold (zero LLM calls during
ingest, the gate still rejects fabricated evidence and deterministic-predicate
writes, reads still run under an exploding gateway).

source_refs.excerpt:
ledger phase 2: the project ledgers itself

The self-hosted ledger goes live: MATTERS.md at the repo root is generated
from assertions distilled out of this repository's own history, and anyone
can reproduce it without an LLM key:

  mh import ledger/assertions.json --db ledger/dev.db && mh matters dev

- Extraction robustness, motivated by live runs: prompts now assign each
  message a short alias (m1, m2, ...) and the extractor maps citations back
  to real record ids deterministically — the gate contract is untouched, and
  a qwen3:4b-class model that previously failed every citation now has a
  fair chance while fabricated aliases still die at the gate. Extraction is
  batched (thread-respecting) instead of one giant prompt per container.
- Provider portability, motivated by DeepSeek: response_format degrades
  json_schema -> json_object -> none on providers that reject strict schema
  (the gate is the real enforcement; the API-level schema is an optimization),
  and both prompts pin their output envelope with a literal example — losing
  server-side schema enforcement no longer lets a model invent envelope keys.
  MATTERHORN_TIMEOUT is formalized with validation and tests.
- mh export --format markdown renders matters with collapsible timelines,
  clickable evidence links, and visible [human correction] badges;
  deterministic byte-identical output from identical state.
- .github/workflows/ledger.yml: nightly + manual, rebuilds the projection
  from the committed assertion export, fills incrementally, commits only on
  change; credentials from secrets, fail-fast when absent.
- Ledger content from the first real fill (DeepSeek): 14 records -> 14 cards
  accepted by the gate -> 42 assertions -> 14 matters, every timeline entry
  linking to its commit. Verified: rebuild-from-export renders byte-identical
  MATTERS.md, and a no-new-commits nightly cycle produces zero diff.

test: assert CLI contracts, not rendered layout

The third environment-dependent failure in this suite. CI failed on all three
Python versions because a test asserted that '--backend' appears in Rich's
rendered help output; at 80 columns Rich wraps the flag across lines and the
substring is simply not there. Reproduced locally with COLUMNS=60.

The tests now normalise help output before asserting, so they check that the
CLI documents its contract rather than checking how Rich happened to lay it
out. CONTRIBUTING.md now states the rule, since this class of defect has now
cost three rounds: tests must not assert on rendered layout, machine-specific
paths, or anything else that varies with the runner's environment.

Verified: 104 passed both in a wide terminal and under

source_refs.excerpt:
M1: deterministic engine core, SQLite store, query family and CLI

Card-level ingest -> assertions -> intervals -> materialized memory cards,
with the read path deriving answers by query alone (P4/INV-10).

Design decisions worth calling out, each traceable to a production bug the
proposal records:

- INV-4 (blocker/next_step/due flicker): a field being absent means "no
  observation", never "cleared"; explicit clearing is expressed by
  EpisodeCard.cleared_fields. The condition that emits a RETRACT and the
  condition that updates the projection are one shared function, not two
  copies that can drift, and re-asserting the same value keeps the existing
  interval open instead of closing and reopening it.
- INV-5 (two unrelated matters merged into one card): merging requires an
  absolute floor of two shared sources; a single shared message is never a
  merge reason, no matter what share of the new card's evidence it represents.
- INV-8/INV-9: SINGLE conflicts resolve on (valid_from, origin, recorded_at,
  assertion_id) with human origin outranking model, and every resolved
  conflict is counted and reported rather than silently discarded.

The core carries no domain vocabulary: it executes any valid SchemaProfile,
and ships two genuinely different profiles (org-matters, personal-decisions)
so the abstraction is driven by more than one case.

source_refs.excerpt:
ledger: break the self-feeding loop, pin batch size, refresh content

Two consecutive CI runs each produced a commit: run two ingested run one's
own 'ledger: nightly update' commit as development activity — the ledger was
ledgering its own bookkeeping, one new matter per night, never converging.
Bookkeeping commits (the github-actions bot author, or the workflow's fixed
message) are now deterministically excluded from ingestion, with tests.

Extraction batches default to five records: at eight, a live DeepSeek run
returned an empty card list for one whole batch — half the history silently
missing from the ledger with nothing in the drop reasons. Five-record batches
produced full coverage (15 records -> 15 gated cards -> 45 assertions).

Ledger content regenerated from the clean fill; every matter's timeline links
to its commit, and the reproduce loop (import committed assertions -> render)
remains byte-identical.

source_refs.excerpt:
M6: the asset becomes a trigger — events, export/import, daily flush

Completes the output surfaces of the brief's §15.2: every output keeps the
three properties (traceable / replayable / deterministic).

- Change events are DERIVED FROM PROJECTION DIFFS, never a second write path:
  after each rebuild the previous interval set is diffed against the new one.
  Assertions stay the only source of truth (P7); events are reproducible
  artifacts with deterministic event_ids, so replay() — which rebuilds the
  same intervals — emits zero new events (P9). Types: matter_created,
  status_changed(from/to), matter_completed, blocked/unblocked,
  decision_adopted, value_corrected; every event carries origin and
  source_ids, so a human correction is visible as origin=human in the stream.
  Queryable (engine.events / GET /v1/scopes/{id}/events / mh events) and
  pushable (mh serve --webhook-url, at-least-once with bounded backoff,
  consumers dedupe by event_id).
- Export/import: mh export produces a versioned, self-contained envelope
  (profile, subjects, assertions — the asset); mh import into an empty store
  reproduces byte-identical projections and query answers, corrections
  surviving with origin intact. Ownership of the memory asset is a deliverable,
  not a promise.
- Service mode gains daily_flush_at alongside the quiet-period loop; embedded
  stays host-driven.
- M5 acceptance defects fixed: unknown task/scope/subject return structured
  404s instead of tracebacks; synchronous wait=true responses now carry
  task_id.

Verified: 190 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17 (47 golden cases);
narrow-terminal green; ruff clean; journey -> correction -> events -> export ->
import -> replay round trip run by hand with identical results and a stable
event count.

M2+M3: distillation gate, protocol surfaces, adapters, PostgreSQL and release

Write path (the only place a model is allowed to run, P1):
- LlmGateway SPI (OpenAI-compatible / Anthropic / null) behind an async dream
  queue. ingest() never calls a model; dream() drains the queue and re-projects
  inside one transaction (INV-6).
- A validation gate with named, counted rejection reasons (P3). The load-bearing
  one is SOURCE_NOT_TRACEABLE: a candidate's cited sources must be a subset of
  the originating card's evidence, so the model cannot invent provenance. The
  same traceability check backs the message->card adapter — one implementation,
  not two.
- Gated creation of non-primary child subjects, which is what makes the
  flagship profile's one semantic predicate (decision_adopted on DECISION_SLOT)
  reachable at all. Child keys are derived deterministically, so a replayed
  dream creates no duplicate subject.

Read path: MCP server on the official SDK (seven tools), FastAPI REST 1:1 with
those tools, and a Claude Skill. All three share one service layer, and none of
them can reach the distill package — enforced by an import-graph test.

Storage: a second backend. PostgreSQL exists to prove the spec is implementable
twice, so the entire conformance suite runs against both, and ordering is
pinned to bytewise (COLLATE "C" / BINARY) rather than the server's locale — a
spec whose answers depend on a deployment's collation is not a spec.

Release: adapters for ReMe/OpenViking digests, four runnable examples including
the human-correction flow, Docker, docs, and CI with the cross-backend
conformance suite as a required gate against the two implementations drifting.

Verified: 138 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17, on both C and
en_US.UTF-8 collations; mh conformance run passes 37/37 on both backends and
exits non-zero on a seeded failure.

# Project strategy

## Layer and promise boundary

Matterhorn is a deterministic, evidence-backed temporal memory layer for
agents. Messages enter on the write side; projected matters and their history
come from persisted evidence rather than generation at answer time. The project
positions this as an L3 layer that complements broad L1 capture and retrieval
tools: Matterhorn accepts traceable upstream material and adds closed
predicates, bi-temporal assertions, deterministic projection, replay, and
first-class human correction.

Sources:
[README — project description and promise boundary](../README.md#the-promise-boundary),
[Positioning alongside L1 memory tools](../docs/positioning.md),
[SPEC — principles](../spec/SPEC.md#1-principles).

## Name and package

The public distribution name is `matterhorn-memory` on PyPI. The Python import
name remains `matterhorn`, as shown by the SDK entry point
`from matterhorn import Engine`.

Source:
[README — installation and SDK entry point](../README.md#five-minute-journey).

## Two-verb facade

The default SDK facade is deliberately centered on two verbs:
`add(messages)` for writes and `matters(scope_id)` for reads. `add()` persists a
task without calling an LLM and `flush()` runs the queued write pipeline;
`matters()` is a deterministic projected read and never calls an LLM. Direct
card and Record ingestion, detailed temporal queries, and correction remain
progressively disclosed advanced surfaces.

Sources:
[README — Two-verb SDK](../README.md#two-verb-sdk),
[README — Progressive disclosure](../README.md#progressive-disclosure),
[CHANGELOG 0.5.0](../CHANGELOG.md#050---2026-07-29).

## Thread-first identity

A communication thread is the first deterministic matter boundary. Identity
does not depend on a model choosing a subject. Cross-thread evidence merging
still obeys the evidence threshold, including the absolute rule that a single
shared source never causes a merge.

Sources:
[CHANGELOG 0.4.0](../CHANGELOG.md#040---2026-07-29),
[SPEC — evidence-based identity merge](../spec/SPEC.md#2-invariants).

## Evidence revocation, not conclusion deletion

Edited Records append new observations and assertions. Deleting or revoking a
Record does not mutate or remove the immutable assertions, intervals, or
materializations it supported. Queries keep the conclusion visible while
marking each source as active or revoked and reporting aggregate evidence
status.

Sources:
[SPEC — INV-11 immutable source lifecycle](../spec/SPEC.md#2-invariants),
[CHANGELOG 0.4.0](../CHANGELOG.md#040---2026-07-29).

## Dual-backend conformance

SQLite and PostgreSQL implement the same Store boundary. Backend-specific SQL
and value normalization stay inside the Store layer, and a behavioral
difference between the two backends is a defect. Both backends run the same
language-neutral golden conformance cases. The current public suite contains
47 cases.

Sources:
[SPEC — PostgreSQL Store and consistency boundary](../spec/SPEC.md#19-postgresql-store-and-consistency-boundary),
[SPEC — Reference conformance harness](../spec/SPEC.md#20-reference-conformance-harness),
[README — conformance suite](../README.md#the-promise-boundary).

## Current milestone

The latest release listed in the changelog is 0.6.0, dated 2026-07-29. It adds
deterministic projection-diff events, at-least-once webhook delivery, versioned
scope export/import, service-only daily UTC flushing, and four output-surface
conformance cases that bring the suite to 47.

Source:
[CHANGELOG 0.6.0](../CHANGELOG.md#060---2026-07-29).

[CHANGELOG 0.5.0](../CHANGELOG.md#050---2026-07-29).

## Thread-first identity

A communication thread is the first deterministic matter boundary. Identity
does not depend on a model choosing a subject. Cross-thread evidence merging
still obeys the evidence threshold, including the absolute rule that a single
shared source never causes a merge.

Sources:
[CHANGELOG 0.4.0](../CHANGELOG.md#040---2026-07-29),
[SPEC — evidence-based identity merge](../spec/SPEC.md#2-invariants).

## Evidence revocation, not conclusion deletion

Edited Records append new observations and assertions. Deleting or revoking a
Record does not mutate or remove the immutable assertions, intervals, or
materializations it supported. Queries keep the conclusion visible while
marking each source as active or revoked and reporting aggregate evidence
status.

Sources:
[SPEC — INV-11 immutable source lifecycle](../spec/SPEC.md#2-invariants),
[CHANGELOG 0.4.0](../CHANGELOG.md#040---2026-07-29).

## Dual-backend conformance

SQLite and PostgreSQL implement the same Store boundary. Backend-specific SQL
and value normalization stay inside the Store layer, and a behavioral
difference between the two backends is a defect. Both backends run the same
language-neutral golden conformance cases. The current public suite contains
47 cases.

Sources:
[SPEC — PostgreSQL Store and consistency boundary](../spec/SPEC.md#19-postgresql-store-and-consistency-boundary),
[SPEC — Reference conformance harness](../spec/SPEC.md#20-reference-conformance-harness),
[README — conformance suite](../README.md#the-promise-boundary).

The latest release listed in the changelog is 0.6.0, dated 2026-07-29. It adds
deterministic projection-diff events, at-least-once webhook delivery, versioned
scope export/import, service-only daily UTC flushing, and four output-surface
conformance cases that bring the suite to 47.

fix(cli): honest exit-code contract and a terminal correction path

Both defects were masked by a fabricated dependency: a previous build could not
download Typer and installed a 103-line hand-written stub into the venv under
the name `typer 0.0.0+verification`. Every CLI test had been passing against
that stub. The venv has been rebuilt with real Typer 0.27.0, which is how these
surfaced.

- `mh conformance run` now exits 0 when all cases pass, 1 when cases run and
  some fail, and 2 when the suite itself is unusable. It previously raised
  click.exceptions.Exit(2), which the stub honoured and real Typer does not, so
  an unreadable suite exited 1 with a traceback. This command is the CI gate and
  the harness the internal Java implementation mirrors, so its exit contract is
  part of the deliverable, not an implementation detail.
- `mh correct` closes the one surface where the correction protocol was missing.
  P8 makes corrections a first-class part of the core contract and the proposal
  names an unused correction protocol as a top risk, yet an operator at a
  terminal had no way to file one.
- Typer and click now carry lower bounds so a fresh install cannot silently
  pick up an incompatible version.

Verified: 141 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17; the three exit codes
demonstrated for real; a correction through the CLI flips a query answer from
(blocked, model) to (open, human).

M5: the two-verb facade — add(messages) and matters()

The project brief's §15.4 names the north star: mem0 won developers with two
verbs; ours are add and matters. Until now the outer door was the card-level
contract — the engine's internal promise boundary, not a user's entry point.

- engine.add(scope_id, messages): minimal four-field contract
  {id, sender{id,name}, text, sent_at} — exactly the gate's three requirements
  (traceability / time / participant), so the easy door does not weaken P5.
  Message ids are namespaced internally (scope:conversation:id) so colliding
  ids across conversations cannot corrupt INV-5's shared-evidence count.
- Receipts: add returns {accepted, task_id} immediately and never calls the
  LLM inline (P1); flush/wait runs the pipeline; engine.task() exposes status,
  cards produced, new assertions, and the gate's rejection breakdown by reason
  — observability none of the L1 tools offer. Tasks persist in both stores.
- engine.matters() returns ergonomic projected objects (.title .status .owners
  .blocked_by .next_step ...) — zero LLM, straight from the projection.
- Protocol surfaces made isomorphic and resource-style: POST
  /v1/scopes/{id}/messages|cards, GET matters, GET query/*, POST corrections,
  GET /v1/tasks/{id}; MCP gains add_messages (9 tools); CLI gains
  mh add / mh matters / mh flush / mh task, with mh init scaffolding a config
  and an offline fixture demo. Old RPC routes removed — no released users.
- Quiet-period auto-flush in service mode only; embedded stays host-driven.
- ingest renamed add_cards (deprecated alias kept); add_records demoted to
  the advanced layer. README (EN/zh) leads with the five-minute journey; SPEC
  gains the §15.1 admission test as a normative rule, the message contract,
  and receipt semantics; 43 golden cases.

Verified: 174 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17; narrow-terminal
green; ruff clean; the journey run end to end in a temp dir as a new user;
colliding-id and gate-breakdown probes pass; MCP add_messages called over the
real protocol.
